rules.rule: Check for causes of generalised non-itchy rash
rules.problem: Check task; every listed finding is used by a diagnosis rule on this page. Trigger loses 'non-itchy' (see c001). Red box only cross-refers to p82, so no priority rule is needed here.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable tick bite fever (generalised rash page)
rules.problem: 'likely' gives probable; (tick bite OR tick present) AND (headache OR T>=38 OR body pain) is faithful. 'Spotted fever group rickettsial disease' rightly covers both African tick bite fever and boutonneuse fever.

'consider' gives possible, and the >=1-of symptom OR is faithful, but 'unexplained' is dropped. Because Generalized rash is_a Skin lesion, every generalised rash patient with headache, fatigue, cough, etc. gets possible mpox, even when another rule explains the rash.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible drug rash (generalised rash page)
rules.problem: 'consider' gives possible; (<= onset (time_ago 3 months)) means 'started within the past 3 months', which is correct. A closer generalised drug-eruption concept exists (c049).

rules.rule: Diagnose probable secondary syphilis (generalised rash page)
Diagnose possible HIV seroconversion illness (generalised rash page)
rules.problem: 'may be part of' gives possible; syphilis-negative AND HIV-negative AND exposure within 6 weeks matches the Yes branch.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable non-specific viral rash (generalised rash page)
rules.problem: 'likely' gives probable. The No branch is encoded as no exposure OR exposure at least 6 weeks ago, which is faithful.

summary: The rules follow the page closely. Every diagnosis has the right certainty (likely gives probable, consider/may gives possible), and the time windows point the right way under the house onset convention. The most consequential gap is in the mpox rule: 'unexplained' rash is not encoded, so (because Generalized rash is_a Skin lesion) any generalised rash plus one common symptom gives possible mpox. The other gaps are minor: the trigger drops 'non-itchy', and a closer drug-rash concept exists ('Generalized skin eruption caused by drug and medicament').
